privacy_policy_statements: If you’re under 13 years old, please have your parent or guardian fill out the form.
Are you Under 13 or responsible for an under-13-year-old?
If you’re under 13 years old, your access to certain features will be restricted in the interest of protecting your Personal Information.
Roblox is especially committed to protecting the privacy of children.
This part of the privacy policy is just for you.
If you’re under 13 years old, please get permission from your parent or guardian to use Roblox.
You shouldn’t use our Services without their go-ahead.
Parents and guardians – we recommend you supervise your child whenever they’re interacting on Roblox.
We’ve got some tools to help – you can learn about Roblox’s safety features
If you’re under 13 years old and create an account, we ask for some information (which is non-personal information, ) to let you use Roblox.
your username (required). We need this to create your account and run the Roblox Service.
We don’t use your username to identify you outside of Roblox
your password (required). We need this to log you in to your account and to run the Roblox Service
your date of birth (required). We’ll use this information to make sure your account has certain
If you’re under 13 years old, we will only ask you to tell us the information we need to set up or protect your account.
We don’t want more Personal Information

If you give us more of your Personal Information, we will: delete any additional Personal Information we’ve collected from you (unless the law requires us to keep it), turn on age-appropriate protections on your account
You can request that Roblox make changes to your child’s account or allow you to review, delete, or prevent the further collection or use of Personal Information from you or your child.
We comply with the Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act (“COPPA”).
You may share your password with your parent or guardian, but do not share it with others.
Once you have an account, you can add your email address (or your parents’ or guardians’ email address if you are under 13) in case you need to reset your password.

If you’re under 13, you (or your parent or guardian) will have to give billing information, including Personal Information such as: Name of the person responsible for buying Robux Their billing address and contact details, like email or phone number credit card or other payment information

You can buy Robux or premium subscriptions and choose how to pay from our available payment methods. When you pay, you (or your parent or guardian if you’re under 13) will have to give billing information, including Personal Information such as: Name of the person responsible for buying Robux Their billing address and contact details, like email or phone number credit card or other payment information
Users who are age 13 or older can also use audio features on Roblox.
We also may use this data to help us provide a better experience on Roblox and to respond to requests about your account from you or your parent or legal guardian.

Asking questions or getting technical support We collect your email address (or your parents’ or guardians’ email address if you are under 13), username, and any other details you give when you: ask us questions or give us comments

Social Media Links (users 13 and older) You can add links to your other social profiles on your Roblox account. This allows you to share these links with other users. You control who can see the Social Media links associated with your account. When you use these features: we may be able to see information about your social media accounts. If you use your Roblox ID to sign in to a non-Roblox website or service, and later delete your Roblox account, you may lose access to that website or service. Audio features (users 13 and older) If you use Roblox’s audio features, we will monitor, collect, use, and store audio captured through your device: to make our voice-related services safer, including to detect and combat abuse and other harmful activity on our Services, in accordance with applicable law, to inform training and product improvement, and in connection with screen recordings that Creators and Users produce through the Services. For more information about laws that apply in your region, please visit Section 7 of this policy. Location-based Services (users 13 and older) You can choose to use location-based Services if you’re 13 or older. If you agree, we may collect and track geolocation information so that
er feature is only available if you are 13 or older and may not be available in certain locations.
Creator Events (users 13 and older)
Creator events are only available if you are 13 or older.
Subscribing to other features (users 13 and older)
This feature is only available to users who are 13 or over.
collect demographic information (eg, age, location, etc) to provide related uses permitted by COPPA.
We may share your Personal Information, as permitted or required by law, if: ... (including schools or children's services) request that we share it.
If you’re 13 years old or over, you can share your Personal Information through chat, forums, messages or similar ways of sharing on our Service.
We are not responsible for how your Personal Information is used if you shared it yourself.
Roblox has a legitimate interest in providing a safe and secure Service, especially to protect children.
When a child creates an account on Roblox, we may process a username, password, birthdate, and gender (gender is optional).
Separate from account creation, users may optionally provide the user access to the Service and to communicate with the parent about the child’s account (if a parent email was provided).
For example, we may use the parent’s email to send an email notification about the child’s account and an invitation for

We may use the birthdate the child provides when signing up for the Service to determine which features on Roblox the child should have access to and to determine when the child will turn 13 years old and can be given broader access to features on our Service.
For example, we may use the parent’s email to send an email notification about the child’s account and an invitation for the parent to review their child's account and update settings.
